## 1 · Trigger, then fan out
Three triggers, one entry point. **Run Config** freezes `as_of` once and derives the three reporting periods from it.

Nothing downstream is allowed to call `new Date()` — a run that takes two minutes must not compute "last 30 days" against two different todays, and a pinned `as_of` is what makes a test run reproducible.

**The reference date is fixed at 2026-06-30**, not taken from the clock. The sources cover Jan 2025 to Jun 2026, so a run anchored to the real today returns nothing and the dashboard looks broken while the workflow is fine.

Periods: last 30 days, last 90 days, year to date — plus a **custom range** when the webhook body carries `custom_start` and `custom_end`.

## 2 · Collect and normalise
Each source node is **On Error → Continue**: a dead source degrades the run, it does not kill it.

Each normaliser has a `FIELD_MAP` at the top — the only place the source's column names appear. When the sheet turns out to say "Value (GBP)", that is the one line that changes.

Records are never dropped. A broken date is stored with `is_countable = false` and named in the issues list.

## 3 · Skip when nothing changed
**Source Fingerprint** hashes the reference date, the period windows and every normalised record. If a completed run already carries that hash, recomputing could only produce the same numbers.

Refresh and the custom-range button then return instantly instead of spending a model call restating what is already on screen. The skip branch stamps `last_checked_at` on the run it matched, so the dashboard can tell "checked, nothing had changed" from "the webhook never fired".

**Scheduled runs never skip.** The daily history point is the whole purpose of them, and a history with holes on the quiet days is worse than no history.

## 4 · Write the facts once
One POST per table with an **array** body. The Supabase node inserts one row per item

The `runs` row is written first with `status = 'running'`, and only flipped to `complete` at the very end. The dashboard reads the `latest_run` view, which filters on complete — so a half-written run is invisible rather than misleading.

## 4 · Every period, one call
This is the decision the whole build rests on: **a reporting period is data, not a dashboard filter.**

**There is no loop.** The metric engine computes every window in one pass — it is arithmetic over arrays already in memory — and Claude receives all of them in one call, returning one object per period.


Source records are filtered to each window **before** any metric is calculated, so no metric can quietly use a different period.

## 5 · Only aggregates cross this line
**Prepare Claude Input** sends computed metrics and a data-quality block. Not one source record crosses.

Every item Claude returns must cite `metric_keys` drawn from a supplied list. **Grounding Check** holds it to that: anything citing a key that was never sent is moved to `ungrounded_claims` and kept out of the report.

That turns "the insights are grounded" from a claim into a number: **0 ungrounded claims**.

## 6 · Commit
Metrics and insights are written per period.

**Complete Run** fires output and PATCHes `runs.status` to `complete`. That single write is the commit point the dashboard keys off — everything before it is invisible to readers.
